case_schema.capability_selector: capability_id, operation_id set, or domain label; may reference reviewed contracts by prefix
case_schema.capability_ids: optional explicit capability-id list for concrete cases bound to the scope register; a candidate: id keeps the source lineage and does not itself mean admission
case_schema.operation_ids: optional explicit registry operation_id list (e.g. global.settings.list_areas); distinct from runtime/diagnostic entrypoint names such as settings.list_areas
case_schema.scope_revision: optional scope-register revision tag (e.g. 2026-11-17-r1) that this case's inputs were frozen against
case_schema.freeze_state: optional freeze qualifier; frozen_for_implementation means the interface and case conditions below are fixed as the implementation contract, not that G0/G1 admission, live execution, or release has been approved
case_schema.template_case_id: optional link from a concrete instance back to the template/policy row it was derived from
case_schema.account_role_permissions: role/permission class only; never a real identity
case_schema.device_requirements: device class requirements only; no real identifiers
case_schema.authorization_status: recorded | reuse_existing_scope | awaiting_resource_confirmation | awaiting_authorization | not_authorized | n/a
case_schema.criterion_assessment: optional per-criterion assessment map: each key names a frozen criterion and its value is pending | met | not_met | not_applicable (with an explicit applicability reason); a file's mere existence never sets met
case_schema.result: recorded_evidence | awaiting_resource_confirmation | awaiting_authorization | awaiting_design | blocked | pending_execution
case_schema.resource_state: optional qualifier on resource readiness, e.g. user_confirmed_no_bound_device | unknown_awaiting_configuration_check | not_applicable with reason; never marks a row complete
case_schema.execution_outcome: optional observed execution outcome; passed requires matching criterion evidence
case_schema.execution_evidence_refs: optional immutable command/live receipt references; results are not inferred from file existence
case_schema.verified_code_commit: optional exact SDK code commit tested; does not imply current future commits were live-tested
case_schema.case_origin: optional origin of a concrete case; retrospective_binding_to_existing_scoped_evidence records an existing executed scope rather than a new run or new G1
case_schema.wire_eval_scope: optional exact operation_id, sync/async modes, registered envelope layouts, four named synthetic scenarios and derived cell count; a test scope, never an API coverage denominator
case_schema.execution_note: optional explanation of evidence reuse and verification boundary
case_schema.limitations: optional list of remaining capability layers not proved by this case
case_schema.pending_questions: optional scenario-specific unresolved contract/interface questions; planning inputs, not executable assertions or evidence

release_gates.item: product prerequisite: scope/capability matrix reviewed and ratified (no source row left unreviewed); every matrix capability has a recorded disposition
release_gates.notes: needs_review, blocked_source, and unratified items are not admissible evidence and cannot be silently excluded or counted as complete; each must be resolved to a concrete disposition (implement / reuse_official_component / not_an_api / duplicate / deprecated / phase_2) with evidence before release. Engineering checks passing does not satisfy this gate.

release_gates.item: product prerequisite: every required-tier acceptance row implemented, documented, and acceptance-completed per its own criteria; example/CLI required rows exercised; required source-semantic issues dispositioned
release_gates.notes: all required rows must reach recorded_evidence (or an explicitly justified not_applicable disposition), not merely pending_execution/awaiting_*; needs_review/blocked_source/unratified required rows mean the gate fails. The pre-gates are an AND condition with the engineering gates below — green Ruff/mypy/pytest/audit alone does not permit upload.
current pyproject declares 0.1.0a1; the plan states the release version must be proposed after scope/compatibility are fixed, not assumed already published

release_gates.item: PyPI project ownership, publishing identity/permissions, and authorization to upload
release_gates.notes: no upload has been executed; the PyPI account/permissions are not yet confirmed. A public-page check on 2026-11-17 returned 404, which only reflects that-moment visibility and does not guarantee the project name is available. Account/Trusted Publisher can be prepared in advance (https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/creating-a-project-through-oidc/) and the first authorized upload creates the project; the user is not required to provide a token now and nothing is uploaded until the product is complete and the pre-gates pass.

release_gates.item: immutable artifact hashes for the exact release commit
release_gates.notes: hashes identify the verified build; rebuilt artifacts must be re-verified rather than reusing prior hashes

release_gates.notes: must run on the release candidate commit

release_gates.notes: check_artifacts covers layout/metadata only; content-level secret scan is a distinct gate

release_gates.notes: tools/release/verify_installations.py; installation verification is not device/network verification

release_gates.notes: actual Actions checks govern; recorded main CI 43878741197 passed for the diagnostics-v1 merge on 3.12-3.15 but does not cover future release commits

release_gates.item: post-publish index check, download hash match, and install verification from the index
release_gates.notes: only after an authorized upload that itself requires the product pre-gates (REL-PRODUCT-SCOPE-RATIFIED + REL-PRODUCT-REQUIRED-COMPLETE) and the engineering gates to pass; build is not release

Domestic async inspection is scoped to 7 HTTP calls and 6 business calls and has passed the verifier-only offline checks. A real run remains pending. The separate six-CLI scenario has a frozen 20-request budget. Its live execution still requires a separate local selection and receipt.

The user identified the overseas console as Singapore on 2026-11-19 and previously confirmed no bound device. Live device acceptance still needs a known visible target and scoped authorization; a console region alone does not verify SDK business routing or access to any target.

Platform message push requires enabled service, reachable callback, independent secret, target type, and trigger authorization; resource_state=unknown_awaiting_configuration_check because the user stated on 2026-11-17 they do not know the platform message service or which callback entry is usable. Dedup/redelivery semantics must be defined before execution. Domestic header 't' timestamp unit is confirmed milliseconds (5130); the overseas 't' unit, freshness window, the 2s vs ~5s timeout conflict, and ciphertext wording remain unconfirmed. Configuration side effects (App reminder stop, ~2h delay, console test temporarily suspending the original callback) need explicit authorization beyond the prior read-only scope.

Release version is undetermined. PyPI account/permissions and upload authorization are unconfirmed; no upload has been executed. The 2026-11-17 public-page 404 only reflects that-moment visibility and does not guarantee name availability. Account/Trusted Publisher may be prepared now (https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/creating-a-project-through-oidc/) and the first authorized upload creates the project; the user is not required to provide a token now.
New business domains must be bound to concrete acceptance rows and frozen before implementation claims; the per-new-domain wildcard row is a policy placeholder, not a substitute for per-item rows.
